q01.question: What is the current Roblox DevEx rate?
q01.answer: Roblox documents a standard rate of {rateStandard} USD per eligible Earned Robux, which it states as {payout30000Plain} USD for {minimumRobux} Earned Robux. This rate took effect on 5 September 2025 at 10:00 PT.

q02.question: How much is 100,000 Earned Robux in DevEx?
q02.answer: {robux100000} eligible Earned Robux is about {payout100000Plain} US dollars at the standard rate before any payment-provider fees or tax. The same amount would have been {payoutLegacy100000Plain} US dollars under the older {rateLegacy} rate.

q03.question: What is the minimum Earned Robux for DevEx?
q03.answer: Roblox requires a minimum of {minimumRobux} Earned Robux in your account before you can participate in DevEx. Reaching that number is a requirement, not an approval — Roblox still reviews every request.

q04.question: Does every Robux balance qualify for DevEx?
q04.answer: No. DevEx applies to Earned Robux, which Roblox describes as Robux earned through creator activity. Purchased balances, gift card credit and other categories are treated differently, and Roblox decides which portion of a balance qualifies.

q05.question: Why is the DevEx rate lower than the price of buying Robux?
q05.answer: They are two different transactions. Buying Robux is a retail purchase with platform pricing applied; DevEx is Roblox paying a creator for eligible earnings. Neither number predicts the other, which is why this site never mixes them in one result.

q06.question: Can I choose which rate applies to my balance?
q06.answer: No. Roblox determines which portion of a balance falls under the standard rate, the legacy rate for balances earned before 5 September 2025, and the higher rate for qualifying spending by verified United States players aged 18 or over. The comparison here shows what each rate would pay, not a menu you can pick from.

devexFeesAndTaxes.metaDescription: Provider fees, currency spreads and income tax all sit between the DevEx rate and your bank account. Model each with your own figures.
devexFeesAndTaxes.quickAnswer: Three separate things reduce a DevEx payout and none of them is the DevEx rate: your payment provider's fees, the currency conversion spread if you are paid outside the United States, and income tax in your own country. This page lets you model each one with your own numbers. It is not tax advice.

q01.question: Does Roblox take a fee on top of the DevEx rate?
q01.answer: The DevEx rate is what Roblox pays per eligible Earned Robux. The {inExperiencePlatformShare}% platform commission was already applied earlier, when the Robux were earned — it is not applied a second time at cash-out.

q02.question: What tax rate applies to a DevEx payout?
q02.answer: That depends entirely on your country and circumstances, and this site does not state a figure for you. The estimator here uses whatever percentage you enter so you can model your own situation.

q03.question: Why is my bank's conversion different from this site's?
q03.answer: Local-currency figures here use European Central Bank reference rates, which are published once each working day and are not tradable quotes. Banks and payment providers apply their own rate plus a margin.

earnedRobux.title: Earned Robux: What Qualifies for DevEx
earnedRobux.metaDescription: Earned Robux is not your whole balance. What counts, what does not, and why the distinction decides whether a payout is possible.
earnedRobux.quickAnswer: Earned Robux is the portion of your balance that came from creator activity — players spending Robux in your experience or on your items — as opposed to Robux you bought, received as a gift, or acquired another way. Only Earned Robux can go through DevEx, and Roblox decides which portion of a balance qualifies.
earnedRobux.ogImageAlt: Earned Robux explained: which part of a Robux balance qualifies for DevEx.

q01.question: Is my whole Robux balance Earned Robux?
q01.answer: Almost certainly not. A balance can mix Robux you earned as a creator with Robux you bought or received. Only the earned portion is eligible for DevEx, and Roblox makes that determination.

q02.question: Do Robux I bought count toward the {minimumRobux} minimum?
q02.answer: Purchased Robux are not Earned Robux, so they do not make a balance eligible for DevEx. The minimum refers specifically to Earned Robux.

q03.question: How do creators earn Robux in the first place?
q03.answer: Roblox pays creators {inExperienceCreatorShare}% of the Robux spent on in-experience purchases such as developer products and passes, retaining {inExperiencePlatformShare}%. That {inExperienceCreatorShare}% is what accumulates as Earned Robux.

q04.question: Can group funds be cashed out?
q04.answer: Group funds are held by the group rather than by an individual account, and payouts have to reach a personal account before DevEx applies. Check the current official documentation for how your specific case is treated.

Roblox reviews each request and decides the outcome. There is no legitimate route outside the official programme.

q01.question: Where do I submit a DevEx request?
q01.answer: Through the official DevEx portal linked from the Roblox Creator Hub. A valid DevEx portal account is one of the documented requirements.

q02.question: How long does a DevEx payout take?
q02.answer: Roblox does not publish a guaranteed processing time, so this site does not state one. Any specific number you see quoted elsewhere is someone's anecdote rather than an official commitment.

q03.question: Is there a faster way to sell Robux?
q03.answer: No legitimate one. Services offering to buy Robux or convert a balance outside DevEx generally violate the Roblox Terms of Use and put your account at risk. Never share your Roblox credentials with any third party, including this site.

q04.question: Do I pay tax on a DevEx payout?
q04.answer: A DevEx payout is income, and how it is taxed depends on where you live. This site gives no tax advice and provides an optional estimate field only so you can model your own figure.

methodology.quickAnswer: Every payout figure is Robux multiplied by an exact decimal rate held as a fraction rather than a floating-point number, rounded once at the moment it is displayed. Required-Robux figures always round up. Local-currency values are European Central Bank reference rates with the observation date shown.

q01.question: How many people are playing Roblox right now?
q01.answer: The table totals the players in the experiences Roblox currently ranks, as of the most recent scheduled observation — one every 15 minutes, with its time shown beside the figure. It is not a platform-wide figure: Roblox does not publish a live total, and this site will not estimate one.

q02.question: Why does the chart cover such a short period?
q02.answer: Because that is how long this site has been recording. The window widens on its own as observations accumulate, up to fourteen days. Showing a fourteen-day axis before fourteen days of data exist would be drawing something that was never measured.

q03.question: Do these player counts affect my DevEx payout?
q03.answer: No. A payout depends on your eligible Earned Robux and the documented rate, not on how busy the platform is.

q01.question: Why is there no live RBLX price?
q01.answer: Because showing one usually means embedding a market vendor's script, which would run in your browser on a page that embeds no such script. The page is wired to fetch a price server-side once a provider is configured.

q02.question: Is Roblox profitable?
q02.answer: It reported a consolidated net loss of 185 million US dollars for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, narrower than the 280 million loss a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA of 152 million. Those are the company's own figures.

q03.question: Does the share price affect the DevEx rate?
q03.answer: There is no documented link. Roblox sets the DevEx rate and publishes it; nothing in its documentation ties that rate to the share price. Nothing here is investment advice.

q01.question: How much does Roblox pay developers in total?
q01.answer: 1,503,106 thousand US dollars in 2025, reported as developer exchange fees on its income statement, against 922,821 thousand in 2024. Both figures come from Roblox's filing with the SEC.

q02.question: Is this data live?
q02.answer: No, and no page can honestly claim it is. Roblox publishes these figures once a quarter, so quarterly is the finest resolution that exists. This site runs no data collection and estimates nothing.

q03.question: Where is the Roblox share price?
q03.answer: Not here. A live quote needs a paid market-data feed and a third-party script, and this site publishes no figure it cannot trace to a document. The reported results it reacts to are on this page instead. Nothing here is investment advice.

q04.question: Does a bigger payout total mean a better DevEx rate?
q04.answer: No. The total reflects how much creators cashed out, not what each Robux was worth. The rate per Robux is documented separately and has changed once in the period shown.

robuxTaxCalculator.title: Roblox Tax Calculator: Marketplace Fee on a Sale
robuxTaxCalculator.metaDescription: What you keep after the Roblox platform commission, or what to charge to clear a target. Covers in-experience and Marketplace sales.
robuxTaxCalculator.quickAnswer: The "Roblox tax" is the platform commission, and it depends on what you sold. On in-experience purchases such as developer products and passes you keep {inExperienceCreatorShare}% and Roblox takes {inExperiencePlatformShare}%. On Marketplace avatar items the creator share starts at {marketplaceAvatarItemCreatorShare}% and rises with price, reaching {marketplaceAvatarItemPlatformShare}% at six times the price floor. This is separate from DevEx.

q01.question: How much is the Roblox tax?
q01.answer: On in-experience purchases the creator keeps {inExperienceCreatorShare}% and Roblox retains {inExperiencePlatformShare}%. On Marketplace avatar item sales the base creator share is {inExperiencePlatformShare}%, rising through a documented tier table to {inExperienceCreatorShare}% for items priced at six times the price floor or above.

q02.question: Is the Roblox tax applied again when I use DevEx?
q02.answer: No. The commission applies once, when the Robux are earned. DevEx then converts the Earned Robux you kept. Applying both to the same figure would understate your payout.

q03.question: What is the price floor?
q03.answer: The minimum price for an item category, which the progressive tiers are measured against. Because floors differ by category, this calculator asks for the multiple rather than assuming one universal floor.

robuxToUsd.title: Robux to USD: Creator Payout vs Purchase Price
robuxToUsd.metaDescription: Two numbers answer this. Compare what DevEx pays a creator against what buying Robux costs, and convert any amount with the rate stated openly.
robuxToUsd.quickAnswer: "Robux to USD" has two honest answers depending on who is asking. A creator cashing out eligible Earned Robux receives {rateStandard} USD per Robux through DevEx, so {robux100000} Robux is about {payout100000Plain} dollars. A player buying Robux pays a retail price set by Roblox, which is a different transaction entirely. This page keeps the two apart.

q01.question: How much is 1,000 Robux in USD?
q01.answer: For a creator cashing out eligible Earned Robux, 1,000 Robux is {rateStandardPerThousand} US dollars at the current DevEx rate. That figure is a payout rate, not the price a player pays to buy 1,000 Robux.

q02.question: Can I convert any Robux to USD?
q02.answer: No. Only eligible Earned Robux can be converted through DevEx, and only once your balance reaches {minimumRobux}. Robux you bought cannot be converted back into money.

q03.question: Why does this site not publish a single Robux purchase price?
q03.answer: Roblox prices Robux by package, region and platform, and those prices change. Publishing one universal purchase rate would be inventing a number, so this page explains the distinction and links to the official pricing instead.

q04.question: Is the conversion the same in every country?
q04.answer: The DevEx rate itself is stated in US dollars. Local-currency figures on this site are reference-rate estimates from the European Central Bank, and your bank or payment provider will apply its own rate and fees.

q01.question: How many Earned Robux do I need for 1,000 USD?
q01.answer: {targetRobuxUp} eligible Earned Robux at the current {rateStandard} rate. Dividing {targetUsd} by {rateStandard} gives {targetRobuxExact}, and the result rounds up so the payout actually reaches the target.

q02.question: How many Earned Robux do I need for 100 USD?
q02.answer: 26,316 Earned Robux would reach 100 dollars arithmetically, but that is below the {minimumRobux} minimum, so you would need {minimumRobux} before a request can be submitted at all — which pays about 114 dollars.

q03.question: Does this tell me how much Robux I can buy for a dollar amount?
q03.answer: No. This page answers the creator question: how much you need to earn to receive a given payout. Buying Robux is priced separately by Roblox and this site does not invent a universal purchase rate.

q04.question: Does the answer change if part of my balance is legacy?
q04.answer: Yes. Legacy balances convert at {rateLegacy}, so reaching the same dollar target takes more Robux. Use the split mode on the calculator to model a mixed balance.
